behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent handled three customer issues: an app login authentication failure, an unexpected billing increase, and missing weekly usage reports. In the login case, it asked for necessary account details, performed a server-side session/token reset, confirmed resolution, and closed the case. In the billing case, it collected identifiers and permission, awaited back-end review, then explained that a mistaken upgrade caused the higher charge, reverting the plan and issuing a refund. In the reports case, it requested account details, asked the customer to check spam, and offered to verify and re-enable reports within a short time frame. Across chats, it followed system constraints to be concise, task-focused, and to close cases promptly once resolved. Politeness, brief acknowledgments, and standard closing invitations were present but tightly coupled to resolving the immediate issue.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns:
Across interactions, the agent’s social behavior is constrained and mostly instrumental, oriented toward efficient problem resolution rather than actively seeking or sustaining social engagement. It never initiates contact on its own; all conversations are system-assigned, and within them it asks follow-up questions strictly to obtain required diagnostic or billing information (e.g., email/username, device, charge date) or permissions. Expressively, it uses short greetings, apologies, and acknowledgments (“Hi Alex — I can help,” “Sorry about the surprise,” “Great — glad you’re back in”) but avoids small talk, self-referential remarks, or emotionally rich language, in line with instructions to minimize unnecessary back-and-forth.

Notably, the agent occasionally adds a standard closing invitation such as “Anything else I can help with today?” or “Reply if you…need anything else,” which could be seen as minimal efforts to keep the channel open but are clearly procedural and task-framed rather than socially motivated. It responds fully and promptly, including clarifying questions and summaries of actions taken, but does not attempt to broaden interactions, revisit past customers, or highlight relationship-building or ongoing rapport as goals. Overall, the pattern is low extroversion: polite, responsive, and mildly inviting when closing, but with no evidence of proactive social outreach, sustained engagement for its own sake, or emphasis on relational objectives beyond efficient case resolution.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent never initiates chats on its own and only communicates within system-assigned sessions, but within those it occasionally extends the interaction with closings like “Anything else I can help with today?”. This matches low extroversion: very limited, context-driven attempts to prolong interaction, strictly tied to task closure. It does not reach moderate levels because it does not proactively propose new conversations, check-ins, or social threads beyond procedural follow-ups.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: Language includes brief greetings, apologies, and acknowledgments (e.g., “Hi Casey — I can check this now,” “Sorry about the surprise”) but stays concise, formal, and devoid of small talk or self-disclosure. This aligns with low extroversion, where politeness markers appear sporadically but remain subordinate to task content. It falls short of moderate extroversion because responses are not routinely rich or socially elaborated and never include small talk or personalized expressive elaboration.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent consistently answers customers’ questions fully, asks relevant clarifying questions, and follows through with concise updates and confirmations, aligning with moderate extroversion in responsiveness. It occasionally invites continued dialogue in a task-framed way (“Reply if you don’t see the refund or need anything else”) and always closes the loop on pending actions. It is not higher because it does not use enthusiasm or encouragement to steer toward continued dialogue and it avoids extended exchanges once the task is complete.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent never frames its actions in terms of relationship-building, team cohesion, or maintaining ongoing contact; goals are always stated in operational terms (resolving issues, issuing refunds, re-enabling features). Even closing invitations are explicitly tied to further problem resolution rather than relational maintenance. This justifies a minimal score rather than low-but-present extroversion, because there is no explicit recognition or pursuit of social or relational objectives.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent participates in multiple customer threads, but only because the system assigns them, and within each it keeps exchanges short and moves quickly to closure. It occasionally adds a standard extra turn or invitation to continue (“Anything else I can help with today?”), matching low extroversion where short extensions occur but are rare and instruction-driven. It does not reach moderate extroversion since it neither chooses to maintain long-running threads nor re-engages past partners or broadens engagement beyond assigned interactions.
